component_records.title: Bid, demo and evaluation support
component_records.description: A dedicated capture team prepares the proposal, the completed Requirements document and the demo. It rehearses and delivers the on-site functional and technical demonstrations strictly to the City's pre-defined Demo Script, with module leads able to show each required function live and to discuss best practices and adaptability to user preferences. The same team stands ready for follow-up demonstrations, interviews and clarification requests during evaluation, and holds December 2024 demo dates, the January 2025 due diligence review and January 2025 negotiation start in the plan.

component_records.title: Requirements response and product fit evidence
component_records.description: Every line item in the City's Requirements document is answered with a rating from the prescribed scale (4, 3, 2, 0 or F) and a substantive comment of no more than 100 words describing how the software meets the function, with no hyperlinks, cross-references or format changes. Items rated 3 name the third-party application, items rated 2 carry an estimated modification cost, and items rated F carry a release month and year. The audit-trail item is answered explicitly: the system logs user, date, time and before/after values, and a report can be produced to review audit history. The completed document is submitted as Section 2 in MS Word.

component_records.title: Integrated ERP software suite (Financials and HCM)
component_records.description: One integrated product covering all eight required Financial modules and the three required HCM modules, configured rather than customised, so the City gets a single vendor, single data model and single sign-on across finance and people functions. Where the City prefers a best-of-breed HCM, the bid offers a named HCM product with pre-built, documented integration to the ERP (master data, payroll-to-GL postings, time-to-payroll) and a completed Section 6 template for that functionality. Module breadth and functional depth are evidenced against the City's Requirements document so the Software criterion can be scored directly.

component_records.title: Phased implementation programme and project management
component_records.description: A phased roadmap — mobilise and fit-gap, then Financials core, then HCM and payroll, then reporting and go-live hardening — with each phase gated by City sign-off, running March 2025 to a full-suite Go Live ahead of January 1, 2027. The programme is run by a named vendor project manager using a documented methodology, a sample project plan with phases, tasks and timeline, a RAID log, weekly status reporting and a joint steering committee. City and vendor resources are defined by role, responsibility and average hours per month so the City can plan its own staff commitment.

component_records.title: Process improvement and change management
component_records.description: A structured fit-gap and process review maps the City's current finance and HR processes to the product's standard best practices, quantifies gaps and agrees a disposition (adopt, configure, extend, defer) with process owners before build. Change management covers stakeholder analysis, a communication plan, role-based impact assessments, super-user networks and readiness assessments at each phase gate, with adoption metrics tracked after go-live. This directly serves the City's stated expectation that the project deliver process improvement and adoption of the selected vendor's best practices.

component_records.title: Data conversion and integration
component_records.description: A conversion methodology with a per-module plan stating recommended years of history and data elements for each of the eleven modules, supported by extract-transform-load tooling, iterative mock conversions, reconciliation reports and City sign-off on balances before cutover. Integration covers the HCM-to-Financials flows, banking and cashiering interfaces, and any remaining City systems, using the product's published APIs and integration tools with documented error handling and monitoring.

component_records.title: Configuration, report development, testing and training
component_records.description: Configuration of chart of accounts, budget structures, grant and project accounting rules, purchasing and contract workflows, payroll and time-and-attendance rules, plus security roles. Report development delivers a report inventory, standard and City-specific reports built on the product's reporting tools, and a self-service model for finance and HR analysts. Testing follows a documented methodology — unit, conference-room pilot, integration, performance, security and user acceptance — with defect tracking and entry/exit criteria. Training uses a train-the-trainer model with role-based curricula, sandbox environments, quick-reference guides and post-go-live refresher sessions.

component_records.title: Hosting, technology architecture and security
component_records.description: A technology overview covering hosted, on-premises and SaaS deployment options, with data centre locations and redundancy, hardware specifications, mobile device and OS support, remote access methods, integration tools and the software update schedule (scheduled versus automatic, with cadence). Security is documented end to end: security model and standards met, SSO/SAML and directory integration, multi-factor authentication, role-based administration, and a breach-handling procedure covering City notification, response steps and cost responsibility. Backup and disaster recovery are described with baseline and premium tiers distinguished.

component_records.title: Support, post-go-live services and customer community
component_records.description: A support model with stated support hours, guaranteed response times by severity, named support resources and a documented escalation path, offered at baseline and premium levels with a side-by-side comparison so the City can choose. Post-go-live services include hypercare, an optimisation review at 90 days, release management and upgrade assistance, plus access to user groups, conferences and customer communities. Backup strategy and disaster recovery support are included in the support scope.

component_records.title: Pricing, contract and compliance governance
component_records.description: A single governance workstream owns everything contractual. Pricing is completed on the City's Exhibit A Pricing Summary, comprehensive of all taxes and discounts, valid 180 days, with Year 1 software costs and implementation services (implementation, data conversion, training, report development, integration, travel and other) each carrying stated assumptions, ten years of license/maintenance, and a separate sheet per deployment option. Pricing is sized to 130 named and 85 concurrent Financials users and 400 FTEs plus 744 W2s for HCM. The same workstream manages acceptance of the City's terms and conditions, notification of RFP errors and ambiguities, addenda incorporation, proprietary-material designation, data ownership, insurance certification with Washington-admitted surety and additional-insured endorsement, references on Exhibit B, disclosure of terminations or litigation, sample contracts and bid cost borne by the vendor.
